restore

/ri-STOR/ — rhymes with door, stress on second syllable · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To restore something is to repair it and bring it back to its original, good condition.

The historical society restored the weathered bandstand until it matched the old photographs exactly.

Example

The conservation team spent months carefully restoring the deteriorated library mural, bringing back its vivid colors and detailed brushwork.

Restore captures the idea of returning something to its original good condition, not just repairing it to function again. Repair alone would miss the sense of returning it to former beauty.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

renovate: Renovate means to update and repair an old building; updating pushes it forward into something newer, with modern wiring or a fresh layout. Restore looks the other way: to restore is to bring a thing back to its original condition, exactly as it once was.

refurbish: Refurbish means to clean, brighten, and spruce up something worn - new paint, new upholstery, a surface freshening. Restore goes deeper than looks: to restore something is to return it fully to its original, good condition, inside and out.

mend: Mend means to patch up something torn or broken so it works again - you mend a fence, a sock, even a friendship. Mending stops at making it whole. Restore goes further, bringing the thing all the way back to its original condition and appearance.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

demolish: to knock down or destroy completely

ruin: to damage something beyond good condition

Where it sits · how completely the original comes back — fix → repair → restore → reconstruct

fix vs. restore: Fix is weaker than restore: fixing something just gets it working again, while restoring it brings back its full original condition.

repair vs. restore: Repair is a step below restore — a repair patches the damage, but to restore something is to return every detail to its original good state.

reconstruct vs. restore: Reconstruct is stronger than restore: restoring means carefully bringing back what remains, while reconstructing means building the whole thing over again almost from scratch.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back, again (Latin)

Root — store

Root — store: to set up, make firm (from Latin staurare)

Put it together

Put it together: Restore joins re- ('back, again') with store ('to set up, make firm' — from Latin staurare): to restore something is literally to set it up firmly again — repairing it back to its original, good condition.

Use the root in a new word: restaurant

Use the root in a new word: restaurant: A restaurant got its name because a hearty meal was said to restore — set firm again — a tired traveler's strength.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Restore is about bringing something back to its original good condition. Use it when repair alone doesn't capture the idea of returning to the former state. For something brand new being made beautiful for the first time, create or build works better.
